utterances.text: I think you have already said that these two last reports, the inventory and the evaluation, are not necessarily prepared by the police officer who conducted the search and seizure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That can be the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And in fact these two reports may be prepared by a police officer who did not prepare the record or the first report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, and that is what happened here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we will rise now and come back at 4.30. (4.00 pm) (A short break) (4.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly remind the witness he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Navrat, may I remind you you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Before the break, we were talking about some of the documentation that is prepared in connection with a search and seizure. The purpose at this point is to become familiar with some of this paperwork, because most of us in this courtroom are not familiar with Austrian police procedures, so I am not necessarily talking specifically about the matter you are here to testify about, I would like to speak for the next couple of minutes about the documents generally. So far, we have seen that there is a document called the record, and so far we have looked at three types of reports, the house search report we have gone over, the report we have called the inventory, and the report we have called the evaluation. Just before we broke off we were talking about the two last reports, the inventory and the evaluation. I believe my last question was that these last two reports, the inventory and the evaluation, are prepared in part on the basis of the record and of the report called the house search; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: As well in preparing these last two reports, police officers examine the allegedly seized items; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In regards to all three reports, the property owner or his representative is not present when those reports are prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So this person does not sign the reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And he does not receive a copy of the reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Just to confirm what you said earlier, these reports are used as proof before the courts to show how a particular search and seizure was carried out and how seized property was controlled while in police custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In short, it is to see whether the search and seizures are legal, is that fair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That can probably already be gleaned from the record because the reference to the legal basis in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: These reports are also prepared to show whether the evidence is reliable; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the further analysis serves to indicate to the court which objects are relevant to the case and to provide the court with those objects.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Aside from being relevant, it shows how reliable the evidence is, whether it came from where we said it came, things like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The paper trail is supposed to start at the premises and end in the courtroom to show that there is some sort of reliability regarding where the evidence came from and how much faith we can put in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would take it that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: My last question on the Bericht, they, as you said, are all required by law, the preparation of the reports are all required by law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not right. What is provided for in the law is listing the objects seized in the inventory, and also to provide the person concerned with a document about the search.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: All right. I would like to move on to another set of questions. Aside from the alleged search and seizure at INDA-Bau, you know there was also searches and seizures carried out at Taubergasse 15 in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At about this same time there were other searches that were being carried out, but with regard to the specific addresses I am afraid I cannot help you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You have already indicated, and we have already seen that your signature appears on the record prepared in connection with INDA-Bau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did put a sort of signature on it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And your signature also appears on the report, the house search, which is prepared in connection with INDA-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I believe you said that you were not a part of the planning of this operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But you would agree with me that this was a well manned and well planned operation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really judge that, because I had to go to carry out this search on short notice, and I am not at all aware as to how the search, the operation was planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But you were well manned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For this search I did have staff along, as said, officers from the 16th District of Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you had enough competent men with you to do this search properly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I assume things went smoothly and there was no pressure on you to hurry operations, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no incidents in the course of the search and there were no consequent complaints tendered to the police concerning it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Let us go back to INDA-Bau for a second. I have a few questions about the allegedly seized items. You say that some documents were seized at INDA-Bau, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A large number of documents were seized that were to be found in these folders.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It is clear from what you said on direct that these documents were not marked before being taken away from the premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You do not know how many documents there were in total?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you certainly have no idea how many pages there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I thought I heard you say that allegedly, there were videos seized at INDA-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the videos were not marked before you left the premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not marked either, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You say these items were brought back to police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These objects were taken to the office where Mr. Panzer is stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You brought these items back in a cardboard box; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The video tapes were in a cardboard box and the folders were in a plastic bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So there was one bag and one box; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What were the dimensions of that box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am afraid I cannot tell you that at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You do not recall?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That must be a standard cardboard box for the police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a standard cardboard box, there is all different kinds of sizes. I am afraid today I can no longer tell you exactly what size it was. At all events, it was big enough for the video tapes to fit in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So it was just an average size box.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This cardboard box was not marked before leaving INDA-Bau, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not marked either, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This cardboard box was not sealed in any way before leaving INDA-Bau, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not sealed, nor was there any insistence that it be sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: My understanding is that the flaps were intertwined on the box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you whether that is the case or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So the box may have been wide open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been open as well, and the plastic bag might have been on top of it with the folders in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the plastic bag was not marked in any way, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not marked either, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And it was not sealed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So nothing prevented anyone from easily opening the bag or the box to have access to the contents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If you have a wide open box or intertwined flaps and a plastic bag that is not sealed, there is not much between the contents and the outside world, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These objects, the objects that I seized, were in custody from the moment I took them until they were brought and delivered to the police station. They were in my custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That was not my question. My question was that both the bag and the box could be easily opened. He did not answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That was not the question, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is an inference, it could be opened. What do you want to ask the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to talk specifically about the trip from INDA-Bau to police headquarters. Did you and your colleagues return to police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Along with you came the allegedly seized items from INDA-Bau; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Who had care and control of these items during this trip from INDA-Bau to police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The objects were under my control.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At what time did you arrive at police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can no longer tell you precisely. At all events, it must have been before 4.45 pm, I would assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you would say between 4.30 and 4.45, is that fair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I take it, as I can recall, the search was over by 4 pm, so it takes some 15 or 20 minutes to get back to police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At what time did you leave police headquarters that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that it would be between 1 and 2 pm that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So 1 o'clock on the morning of the next day; is that correct? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: There may have been a problem in translation, so I will ask the question to you one more time. You arrived at police headquarters between 4.30 and 4.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us narrow down the question; 4.30 or 4.45 pm, is it? So he will know from where to take off.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We will say you arrived at 4.45 pm at police headquarters. What time did you leave police headquarters that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I must have reached police headquarters by 4.45 at the latest. As to when I left police headquarters, I am afraid I no longer remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Was it before midnight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Were you there for one hour, two hours, four hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really say, I am afraid. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It would be more than a hour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But it could have been more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been more, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You say that you brought these items allegedly seized from INDA-Bau to room 326?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The objects which I seized were brought to the office where Mr. Panzer and his group were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That is the office of Moerbaur, Bycek and Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Moerbaur, Bycek and Panzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At what time did you go to that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, it had to be before 4.45 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you went immediately to that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You handed the objects over to Panzer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: When Mr. Moerbaur was here testifying he said you gave the objects to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I placed these objects on Mr. Panzer's desk and I told him that I was done with the search and he took over these objects.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbaur says you gave him those objects in room 331.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know where room 331 is. I brought these objects to the office where Mr. Panzer and his colleagues were housed and I cannot really tell you whether it was 326 or 327, but at all events, it is the room where Panzer and his group were lodged.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbaur describes room 331 as the office he shares with his colleagues. Does that sound right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If that is the room then it might well be room 331, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is that the room where allegedly seized items from the other locations were brought?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What are the dimensions of that room approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I take it it is about between 20 to 30 square metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is there furniture in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are cabinets and a number of desks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The room into which you brought your allegedly seized items, there were also many other people there that evening, were there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Bycek and Mr. Moerbaur might already perhaps have been there, but I can no longer tell you that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Did other people arrive in that room that evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that either, because after I handed over the objects I had seized to Mr. Panzer I went to my office to draw up the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you are saying you just dropped off the objects and left the room; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Then you went off to prepare the report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you have no idea whether they were objects brought in from the other locations in relation to other seizures in this matter; you do not know whether they came that night or not, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You do not know whether the police officers who allegedly performed those other searches and seizures showed up that evening? You never saw them either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can no longer remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Zdravko Mucic that evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am aware that he was taken to police headquarters, but I did not see Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: How long after -- I will come back to that in a second. Let us talk about the documents specifically that you prepared in connection with the alleged search and seizure at INDA-Bau. Aside from the record you prepared or signed, and the report, the house search, which you prepared and signed, you know that there were two other reports prepared as well. Let me help you. One of them was prepared, the inventory, by Bycek and Panzer on April 22nd 1996, and the other report, the evaluation was prepared by Bycek and Panzer again on April 22nd 1996.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know of my record and my report. With regard to the inventory and the analysis report, I cannot tell you anything about it, because I had no further dealings with this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you have never seen those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw these documents when looking through things at the company premises. I have never seen these other two reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You said earlier, I believe, that the alleged search and seizure took place on 18th March; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This search took place on 18th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, could we have the record, Prosecution Exhibit 165 and 165A, shown to the witness, please? (Handed). I also have copies for the three judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I must confess, your Honour, I am confused as to what these documents are. I thought the usher was asked to show the witness the Prosecution exhibit. Unless my friend has copied the Prosecution exhibit, I do not know what he is now showing your honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I do not know if we can have it marked as a Delalic exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I certainly have no problem with the witness being shown a Prosecution exhibit, I just do not know what this document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: An exhibit is an exhibit, part of the record. If a document is already part of the record, you can take advantage of it. Why have it twice exhibited, once as a Prosecution exhibit and again as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is already in the list of exhibits. There is no point, except if there is a difference between the two, and you intend to emphasise the difference, that one can understand, but as long as it is the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It is, your honours. You have the record in front of you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I am looking at the first page. I would like to go over this a little bit with you. Up in the top right of the record we see the date, 19th March 1996, typed in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If we go to the bottom of that first page on the last line, the blank space over the word "date" is not filled in, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So on the face of this document, it shows that the search of INDA-Bau took place on 19th March 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not what it means. The search was carried out on 18th March.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That is what you told me earlier, but you also told me earlier that this document is prepared on the spot, during the search. So on the face of it, it shows 19th March 1996, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already indicated today that this record was handed to me already partly filled out. Apparently, the officers who filled it out expected the search to take place on 19th March and so that is how they gave it to me and I did not check this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But on the bottom line, there is this place for the date which is blank. You could have written in the date, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Are you sure it took place on the date that you said it took place, this search and seizure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am quite sure about that, because I drew up my report about the search and I indicated then what the date was and Mr. Kovanovic, who was present in the premises, was provided with a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But all we have is your word against this document, is that correct, on the date when the alleged search and seizure take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The search took place on 18th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Are you telling me there were two searches; one on the 18th, one on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has already explained it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was only one search, and it took place on 18th March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is there any good reason why you think you need to emphasise the difference in the dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: On the front page again at the bottom on the last line in the blank space over the word "time", which is right next to the blank space over the word "date". It is not filled in, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is nothing written in there either, no, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Again, on the face of the document, we do not know at what time the alleged search and seizure took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to the time, you can find that in my report about the search, when it started and when it was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Again on the front page, moving up to the top line, we see three numbers, 1021, 1874 and 1707. That is where the police officers should be identified, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1021, 1874 and 1707, those are the service numbers assigned by the Vienna police department to the officers in question and those officers were involved in the search.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But nowhere in this document is there a name linked to these numbers, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So again on the face of the document we do not know who conducted the search, do we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the face of the document, no, there is no reference to the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Turning to the second page of your record, I am looking at where you filled in the allegedly seized items. You see there are 51 unmarked cassettes, video cassettes, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And there is a total of 12 unmarked folders or binders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We have seen so far a number of errors in this record that you signed. Did you read it before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The record was drawn up by me, and filled in in part by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you did read it before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I added I certainly reread.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you are saying you did not read it in its entirety before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I had read it in its entirety, then certainly there would be a different date indicated on the front page. I checked to see whether the references were appropriate, to see in connection with whom it was issued and to see for what address it was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Let us move along to the second document on which your signature appears, the report, the house search, which is dated 18th March 1996. Where was the report, the house search, prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The search report was drawn up by me in my office, that is office 322.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At what time did you prepare that report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was subsequent to the search, that is to say subsequent to the delivery of the seized items to Mr. Panzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Do you know what time that was, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that it was after 4.30 pm, or towards 4.30, that I began.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So soon after you arrived at police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Did you prepare this report on the basis of the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the record, but also on the basis of my own notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Did you also inspect the allegedly seized items when you prepared this report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not have any further look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I would like to show a copy of this report to the witness, marked for identification. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is marked as D56/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You are looking at the English translation on the first page, and the last two pages are in the German language. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second and third pages, yes, I recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Those are the ones dated March 18th, 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That is your signature at the end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This is the report, the house search, you prepared in connection with the search and seizure at INDA-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your honours, I move to have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In this document you claim that the alleged search and seizure of INDA-Bau took place on March 18th, contrary to what is indicated in the record; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You make reference to video tapes in this report. They had not been marked at this point, had they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I take it that at the time this report was drawn up the video tapes had not yet been marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So you note 51 unmarked videos, the same number as in the record; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The documents, the folders and files to which you make reference, they had not been marked at this point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So there you note a total of 12 unmarked folders, the same number of folders as appears in the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the same figure, if you add them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: A moment ago I made reference to the report, the inventory prepared by Panzer and Bycek on April 22nd, 1996. That record was prepared in connection with the alleged search of INDA-Bau. With the assistance of the usher, I would like to show that document to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is marked as D57/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Have you ever seen the last two pages of that document, the ones signed by Bycek and Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not recognise these pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You would agree with me, though, that it is the report prepared by those two gentlemen in connection with the alleged search and seizure at INDA-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I take it that Messrs Bycek and Panzer were referring to that search, i.e. the search at INDA-Bau.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You notice if you look at it, it is rather short, that this document does not state on what date the alleged search and seizure at INDA-Bau took place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I suppose in fairness to your colleagues, based on your documents, they could not be sure of the date, could they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I take it that the colleagues knew when the search occurred because at the same time, they were carrying out a search as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This report makes reference to items that were allegedly seized from INDA-Bau, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And this report makes reference to 12 files which for the first time in any document associated with INDA-Bau indicates that they have been identified as I/1 to I/12; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that, because I do not know more about the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You would agree it is the first document we have seen together today that makes any type of identification of the files; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is possible, but I cannot judge the matter because I do not know more about the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This report makes reference to 54 not 51 videos as your previous documents state; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Based on documents you and I have looked at, for the first time, those videos are given an identification, I/13 to I/66; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that because I do not know more about it, but I see that they have been numbered and perhaps also marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Contrary to what your documentation showed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So let us back up for a second and have a look at what you have said about INDA-Bau. You have told us that the allegedly seized items left the premises unmarked, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Certain things were put into a cardboard box that was not marked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The cardboard box was not sealed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The flaps on top of the box may or may not have been shut; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your honours, do we have to go through all of this again?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I am just summarising, your honours. I am almost through.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sure such a summary can be left for final addresses or at some time when the documents are sought to be admitted, your honours, but is it necessary to summarise it again through the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You have about five minutes, any way you wish to present your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We have also seen the date on the record does not correspond to the date you say the search at INDA-Bau took place, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The time is not indicated in the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The time was not indicated in the record, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Based on the record, we do not know the identity of the police officers who allegedly did the search and seizure?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to that, your Honour, because it is not strictly correct. The witness has attested to the fact that the identification numbers of the police officers were put on to the report and has taken us to them. That is a means by which identification can be made of the officers and I object to this question, it is not correctly put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is a question the witness can answer from his own knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The question was; based on the record, you had no way of knowing the identity of the police officers who allegedly conducted the search and seizure alter INDA-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true, because the service numbers are there in the record and you can see who is behind, as it were, those numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In looking at these three documents we have just gone through, the record and the two reports, the allegedly seized items from INDA-Bau may not be the ones that showed up at police headquarters that day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We have gone from 51 to 54 videos, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That is a discrepancy of three, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: One possibility is that three new videos were added to the original 51; you would accept that possibility, would you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everything is possible, but I have a tough time imagining that.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Another possibility is that we are dealing with 54 different videos from the ones that came from INDA-Bau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: They were not marked, the container was not marked. It was not sealed. You accept that possibility, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can rule out that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In fact, the cardboard box which left INDA-Bau may not be the same one that arrived at police headquarters, because it was not marked either?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He did say it was in his custody until he brought it to police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We know for sure that the number of videos inside the box changed, do we not, between the time --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Maybe your colleagues were looking through a different cardboard box.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a tough time imagining that.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If the video tapes changed, perhaps the documents changed, too, between the time you brought it and the time your colleagues examined it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why do you not leave that for the argument stage instead of putting it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: One final question on this point. Earlier we looked at Article 145 of the code together. That article clearly states that items should be sealed before leaving the premises and that was not done here, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These objects are sealed at the request of the person concerned, but no such request had been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I am referring to paragraph 3 of Article 145, which says if a proper inventory cannot be done, it should be sealed, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He did not do that because it was not requested. That is what he just told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have one final question for today, your Honour. You say you saw the folders in front of you that you looked through earlier on 1st August 1997. You saw them on 1st August 1997?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is that when you practiced putting them in the three neat piles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Shall we stop there for today, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Will you wish to continue tomorrow afternoon your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we leave I have a request on behalf of my client. As the court is well aware, Mr. Delic has a bad back and he is hurting quite a bit today. Since it does not appear he is going to be directly affected by the continued testimony of this witness and the next witness, he would ask the Trial Chamber's permission to be excused for coming tomorrow and Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think he could be excused, since you are still here representing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of my client, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Landzo is in the same position other than the back pain. It does not affect him and he has other work he would like to be able to do, if that is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He can be excused. He is in very good company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
